messages:
sarah_marketing: Hey @kevin_runtime / @ajay_ml — we need a clean set of benchmark runs for the webinar next Tue. Marketing wants reproducible numbers + raw logs + a short narrative. Can eng/runtime run the following and drop results in S3?

Checklist we need: model list: redwood-v1-1b, open-llama-7b; sequence lengths: 128, 512, 2048; batch sizes: 1, 8, 32; run with prefix cache ON and OFF; quantization: fp16 and int8 (if supported); metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU mem usage, per-run cost estimate. Also include the exact command(s) + git commit/model hash + any kernel/compiler flags. ETA: ideally initial numbers by Fri EOD. Thanks! :pray:

kevin_runtime: Got it. Can you drop the sample prompt set and the S3 path where you want the outputs? Also which hardware to target? H100 only or include AWS g5/HPC?

sarah_marketing: Link to sample prompts: https://gist.github.com/redwood/bench-sample-2026 (contains 500 prompts, mix of short+long). Put results in s3://redwood-marketing/bench/webinar-2026-03. Please include H100 (on-prem), G5 (aws), and one CPU baseline for cost comparison. Demo will highlight latency vs throughput tradeoffs so both single-shot and streaming/run-level numbers are useful. Also: deterministic seeds please.

ajay_ml: Suggest adding int8 quantized runs and a tiny quality check: compare greedy output similarity on 100 eval prompts (BLEU / chrF or simple token-overlap) so marketing can be confident there’s no huge quality regression. Also set dropout to 0 and fix RNG.

leo_data: I can clean the 500 prompts and upload splits. Will put train/dev/holdout (100 dev, 100 holdout) into s3://redwood-marketing/bench/webinar-2026-03/payloads by EOD today. Will annotate prompt types.

kevin_runtime: TL;DR: we’ll run configs and push raw run logs + perf summaries. Example harness command (we’ll adapt per infra):

```bash
python infra/bench/run_bench.py \
  --model redwood-v1-1b \
  --device h100 \
  --seq_len 512 \
  --batch_size 8 \
  --warm_kv True \
  --prefix_cache False \
  --quantization fp16 \
  --runs 10 \
  --seed 42 \
  --out s3://redwood-marketing/bench/webinar-2026-03/results/redwood-v1-1b/
```

We’ll also capture nvprof traces and kernel logs and a csv per-run. Will include model commit sha and container image id in output metadata.

ci-bot: :gear: CI queued: bench-job-1763854321 for 6 configs. Watch s3://redwood-marketing/bench/webinar-2026-03/ for artifacts.

kevin_runtime: Plan: initial smoke runs on H100/G5 today (smaller set: seq 128/512, batch 1/8) — full matrix (including 2048 and batch 32 + int8) will run overnight and Monday AM. ETA for complete CSV + raw logs: Monday 10:00 AM PT. Is that okay?

sarah_marketing: That works. Acceptance criteria for marketing: either (A) p95 < 120ms for seq128 batch1 on H100 for redwood-v1-1b OR (B) a clear narrative + numbers showing tradeoffs and a cost-per-1M-tokens estimate. Must have raw logs and a one-page summary (table + 3 bullets) we can drop into slides. Also need the exact commands and env for reproducibility.

ajay_ml: Small note: for int8 runs we should include small calibration traces and a brief note if any ops fell back to fp16. I’ll help review the quality check outputs when they land.

kevin_runtime: Acknowledged. We’ll include calibration steps and op-fallback logs. Will tag results with model hash and a "run_metadata.json" containing env, kernel flags, pytorch/torch-version, cuda, and quant backends.

maya_sales: If numbers look good, can we get a 1–2 sentence non-technical blurb for the sales deck? e.g., "Redwood produces X ms p95 latency for low-latency LLMs on H100" — will need legal sign-off later.

sarah_marketing: Yep — marketing will draft a few options once we have numbers.

kevin_runtime: One last ask: please confirm the cost assumptions for cost-per-1M-token calc (spot vs on-demand, node type). I’ll include both.

sarah_marketing: Include on-demand and our committed-dedicated baseline. Use current cloud pricing and our internal H100 equivalent rate.

kevin_runtime: Cool. I’ll start the smoke runs now and post the first CSVs in the S3 path above. I’ll ping this thread when the artifacts are ready. :white_check_mark:

sarah_marketing: Amazing — thank you team! :rocket:
